questions.topic: Resolving a launch velocity
questions.stem: Explain how to resolve a launch velocity into horizontal and vertical components.

answer.exemplar: Multiply the launch speed by cosine of the launch angle for the horizontal component and by sine for the vertical component.

questions.explanation: Components come from right-triangle trigonometry: v_x = v cosθ, v_y = v sinθ. These combine via Pythagoras.

answer.exemplar: Time of flight equals two times the initial vertical velocity divided by g, because ascent and descent are symmetric.

questions.explanation: Vertical motion is symmetric: time up equals time down, so total time is 2 v_y/g. Horizontal motion does not affect it.

questions.topic: Horizontal velocity in a projectile flight
questions.learningObjective: Analyze effect of launch angle on horizontal velocity
questions.stem: For fixed launch speed, how does increasing launch angle affect horizontal velocity?

options.text: It makes horizontal velocity zero always.

questions.explanation: Horizontal component = v cosθ; as θ increases toward 90°, cos decreases. Thus horizontal velocity decreases.
questions.hint: v_x = v cosθ decreases with θ.
